title: 2015 AMC 12B 17
statement: An unfair coin lands on heads with a probability of \(\dfrac14.\) When tossed \(n\) times, the probability of exactly two heads is the same as the probability of exactly three heads. What is the value of \(n?\)

solutions.text:
Setting the two probabilities equal and cancelling the common powers of \(\tfrac14\) and \(\tfrac34\) gives \(\binom{n}{2}\cdot\dfrac34 = \binom{n}{3}\cdot\dfrac14.\)

This becomes \(\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}\cdot 3\) \(= \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6},\) so \(\dfrac32 = \dfrac{n-2}{6},\) giving \(n - 2 = 9\) and \(n = 11.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
